changes: validation-execution-lock.ts: validationExecutionLockPath now roots the per-story lock at the shared git-common-dir root (resolveSharedLockRoot), so all linked worktrees/hosts of one story share ONE lock. done-required-validation.ts + validation-types.ts: command-spec digest uses a repo-root-relative logical cwd (schema v1->v2), buildLegacyAbsoluteCwdCommandSpecEnvelope accepts pre-existing v1 receipts, a non-digested resolvedCwd provenance field, and validateRequiredReceiptCoverage/isPackagesMainBuild compare repo-relative cwd on both sides so cross-host receipts verify. New worktree-portability-smoke.ts (16 checks).
usage: Run validation for the same story from two linked worktrees: they serialize on one shared lock, and a done-required-evidence.json recorded on host A verifies on host B. node packages/main/dist/tasks/worktree-portability-smoke.js proves it.
expectedOutcome: validationExecutionLockPath identical across two worktree roots; digest identical across roots for the same logical command; legacy v1 receipts still verify.
actualTranscript: worktree-portability smoke passed (16 checks); RED 2/2 FAIL->PASS; done-required + freshness + gitroot-cwd suites pass.
outcomeDiff: No difference: the smoke demonstrates exactly the expected portable behavior.
limitations: For an absolute command.cwd that lies ENTIRELY outside any shared filesystem ancestry of the worktrees (e.g. a literal /opt/tool with a symlinked divergent suffix), relative-path portability cannot be reconstructed; same-host same-story behavior is unaffected. Non-git projects fall back to per-root behavior (byte-identical to before).
pitfalls: The command-spec schema bumped v1->v2; consumers reading the digested cwd must expect a repo-relative value, not an absolute path. Legacy v1 receipts remain accepted via the migration path; do not remove buildLegacyAbsoluteCwdCommandSpecEnvelope until all historical receipts are re-validated.
